notes.what_this_is: A record carried by the file and NOT imported: sanitiseState keeps only the fields CONTRACT §6 lists, so nothing below reaches the app. It is here so the derivation of every number above can be checked by a human against the snapshot.

notes.purchase_prices: Fourteen players have been held since GW1 (history.current event_transfers is 0,0,0,0,1), so their purchase price is now_cost - cost_change_start. Exact, T0.

calvert_lewin_purchase.derivation: Bought in GW5 (the only transfer of the season). The transfers endpoint needs a login, so the price is derived, not read. bank went 0 -> 16 tenths across GW4->GW5 with event_transfers_cost 0, so sell(João Pedro) - buy(Calvert-Lewin) = 16 exactly. João Pedro: now_cost 77, cost_change_start 2 -> purchase 75, sell price 76. Hence buy = 76 - 16 = 60, which is also Calvert-Lewin's start price (now_cost 60, cost_change_start 0).
calvert_lewin_purchase.what_would_change_it: The pair (sell 75, buy 59) also satisfies the bank delta. It needs João Pedro to have been 76 or less at the GW5 deadline and Calvert-Lewin to have fallen to 59 by 18 September and recovered to 60 by 26 September. The snapshot carries one price per player, not a price history, so neither is excluded from the data alone. The figure is marked estimated for that reason.

reconciliation.reading: purchase sum + bank = 1001 against the GW5 value of 999: a gap of 2 tenths (£0.2m). history.current[].value is selling value + bank measured at that gameweek's deadline, and a player whose price has fallen sells at his current price, so the gap is the net of the falls and the halved rises as at 18 September. It is not a missing or invented price. Selling value computed on today's prices is 979 (+ bank 16 = 995), four tenths lower again, because Semenyo, Brobbey, Hughes and Shaw have fallen further since that deadline.
reconciliation.not_asserted_exact: The identity value = sell + bank cannot be asserted to the tenth from this snapshot, because the snapshot has no per-deadline prices. What is asserted: the bank delta pins sell(out) - buy(in) exactly, and the gap above is signed and explained.

ledger.basis: Every row is a decision that was on the table, what the app recommended, what he did, what the gameweek actually scored, and the marginal regret. CONTRACT §6 fixes the eight fields; the semantics are: pick = the app's recommendation, alt = what he actually did, outcome = the realised squad points of the gameweek as played (T0, history.current[].points), regret = the marginal squad points the recommendation would have ADDED, so a positive regret means ignoring the app cost him that many and a negative regret means his own call was better. null regret means the app had no recommendation of record for that decision.
ledger.counterfactual: Realised, not modelled. Every player's gameweek points come from data/live.json gw["4"] and gw["5"], which are the event/{gw}/live/ rows (T0). A recommended fifteen was never played, so it has no played eleven: its counterfactual is scored on the HINDSIGHT-OPTIMAL legal eleven with the recommended captain doubled, which makes the squad-level regret an UPPER BOUND. The xi rows isolate his own eleven-and-bench leak on exactly the same hindsight-optimal basis, so the two net: of the 31 on the GW4 chip row, 25 is the squad and 6 is the eleven he picked out of the fifteen he had.
ledger.xp_fields: xp_pick and xp_alt carry the EX-ANTE expectation only where this project recorded one at the time. The only such figure in the memory files is EV_cap 6.1 for João Pedro's GW4 captaincy (CLAUDE.md Part M). Everywhere else they are 0, which means "no ex-ante figure was recorded", not "an expectation of zero". They are not recomputed from today's snapshot: the snapshot carries one price, one status and one cumulative stat line per player, so any ex-ante number rebuilt from it would read the gameweek it is predicting (ERRORS.md E-069).

workings.gw4_wildcard: The fifteen of record (data/weekly.js v88 classic.wildcard15) scored 96 across all fifteen; its best legal eleven in hindsight, 3-4-3 with João Pedro captained, is Raya, Bogle, Tarkowski, Calafiori, Saka, Rogers, Janelt, Scott, João Pedro, Haaland, Barry = 102. He scored 71.
workings.gw4_fallback: The written fallback (Hughes→Yalcouyé, Shaw→Ajayi, Diop→Mendy, three free transfers, no hit) gives a best hindsight eleven of 87 in 3-5-2. He scored 71.
workings.gw4_captain: João Pedro scored 12, Haaland 9. Both were in the eleven, so the armband swap is worth exactly 12 - 9 = 3 squad points.
workings.gw4_xi: The best legal eleven of the fifteen he actually held, Haaland captained, is 77 against the 71 he played: 14 points sat on the bench and 6 of them were recoverable.
workings.gw5_transfer: João Pedro scored 0 in GW5 and Calvert-Lewin scored 2, both as single-count starters, so the transfer he made GAINED 2 and the regret is -2. On the hindsight-best-eleven basis the same comparison reads 66 against 67, a gain of 1.
workings.gw5_xi: The best legal eleven of his GW5 fifteen is 67 against the 62 he played: 8 on the bench, 5 recoverable, mostly Verbruggen 6 benched behind Kinsky 2.

ledger.bench_leak: points_on_bench by gameweek: 3, 4, 14, 14, 8 = 43 over five gameweeks, and the last three are the worst three. The recoverable part, measured as the best legal eleven against the eleven played, is 6 in GW4 and 5 in GW5.
